Trayce Jackson-Davis is an American professional basketball player.
Trayce Jackson-Davis (né Davis) is more commonly referred to by his initials "TJD".
Trayce Jackson-Davis was born on February 22, 2000.
Trayce Jackson-Davis plays for the Golden State Warriors of the NBA.
Trayce Jackson-Davis played college basketball for the Indiana Hoosiers.
Trayce Jackson-Davis was selected 57th overall in the 2023 NBA draft by the Golden State Warriors.
Trayce Jackson-Davis grew up in Greenwood, Indiana.
At age four, Trayce Jackson-Davis fractured his skull in a home accident with a resistance band; surgery left him with scars above both ears.
At age six, Trayce Jackson-Davis had an accident with a golf club that fractured his cheekbone and eye socket, requiring placement of a titanium screw.
In middle school, Trayce Jackson-Davis played on the B team; his play improved after a growth spurt in summer before starting 9th grade.
Trayce Jackson-Davis attended Center Grove High School in Greenwood.

As a junior in 2017–18, Trayce Jackson-Davis averaged 21.9 points, 9.4 rebounds, 4.1 blocks, and 2.6 assists per game while shooting 67.0% from the field; he helped his team to a 20-win season, county and sectional titles, and the 4A regional final.
In AAU basketball with Spiece Indy Heat, Trayce Jackson-Davis averaged 19.1 points, 7.1 rebounds, and 1.8 assists per game while shooting 59.1% from the field.

During his senior season, Trayce Jackson-Davis led Center Grove to a 21–8 record and a berth in the Class 4A state tournament semifinals; he averaged 21.6 points, 9.3 rebounds, 2.9 blocks, 1.7 assists, and one steal per game through 29 games.
Trayce Jackson-Davis entered the state semifinals with 1,768 career points.
On January 24, 2019, Trayce Jackson-Davis was announced as a McDonald's All-American to participate in the 2019 game; he finished with 7 points, 5 rebounds, and 1 block in 14 minutes.
Trayce Jackson-Davis was rated as a four-star recruit by Rivals, 247Sports, and ESPN.
During his high school career, Trayce Jackson-Davis was recruited by numerous high-profile schools including Indiana, Michigan State, UCLA, Ohio State, Purdue, Xavier, among others.
On November 30, 2018, Trayce Jackson-Davis committed to playing college basketball for Indiana after narrowing his choices down to Indiana, Michigan State, and UCLA.
Trayce Jackson-Davis made his college debut for Indiana during the 2019–20 season with eight points and six rebounds in a 98–65 win over Western Illinois.
Trayce Jackson-Davis was named Big Ten co-freshman of the week on November 18, after contributing 20 points, eight rebounds, and three blocked shots against North Alabama.
Trayce Jackson-Davis was again named conference freshman of the week on December 2 after scoring 21 points and grabbing 11 rebounds in a victory over Louisiana Tech.
On February 19, 2020, Trayce Jackson-Davis set career highs with 27 points and 16 rebounds in a 68–56 win over Minnesota.

At the close of the regular season, Trayce Jackson-Davis was named to the Third Team All-Big Ten by the coaches and media as well as the All-Freshman Team; he averaged 13.5 points, 8.4 rebounds, and 1.8 blocks per game as a freshman.
Trayce Jackson-Davis finished second in the league in field goal percentage (56.6%), and seventh in blocked shots (1.9) and rebounds (8.4).
Trayce Jackson-Davis started in each game his freshman season; he was one of only four freshmen in the country to lead his team in scoring, rebounding, free throw percentage, and blocks.
As a sophomore during the 2020–21 season, Trayce Jackson-Davis averaged 19.1 points and 9.0 rebounds per game.

Trayce Jackson-Davis garnered several awards at the close of the 2020–21 season; he was named a third team All-American by the Sporting News, NABC, and USBWA; an honorable mention All-American (AP); All-Big Ten (First Team by media and AP; Second Team by coaches); and a Wooden Award Finalist.
In the offseason prior to Jackson-Davis's junior year, Mike Woodson was hired as head coach of the Hoosiers, and Jackson-Davis announced he was returning for his junior season.
On November 27, 2021, Trayce Jackson-Davis scored a career-high 43 points in a 90–79 win over Marshall; this became the first Indiana player to score at least 40 points in 27 years.
On November 30, 2021, Trayce Jackson-Davis had 31 points, 16 rebounds, and three blocks in a 112–110 double-overtime loss to Syracuse.
Trayce Jackson-Davis was named to the Second Team All-Big Ten and Big Ten All-Defensive Team; as a junior, he averaged 18.3 points, 8.1 rebounds, and 2.3 blocks per game.

Trayce Jackson-Davis became the second player in Indiana history (with Alan Henderson) with 1,500 points, 750 rebounds, and 150 blocks; he ranked 15th on Indiana's all-time scoring list with 1,588 points, ninth in rebounds (797), seventh in blocked shots (178), and seventh in field-goal percentage (55.8%).
On April 9, 2022, Trayce Jackson-Davis declared for the 2022 NBA draft while maintaining his college eligibility.
On May 20, 2022, Trayce Jackson-Davis announced his withdrawal from the draft and his return to Indiana.

Heading into Jackson-Davis's senior year (2022–23), he garnered substantial national recognition; he was named a Blue Ribbon Preseason First Team All-American, Associated Press Preseason All-American, Almanac Preseason Second Team All-American, CBS Sports Preseason Second Team All-American, Big Ten Preseason Player of the Year, Preseason All-Big Ten Team, and The Athletic Preseason Second Team All-American.
His January averages of 23 points, over 14 rebounds, and over three blocked shots were one of only three such months in the last 25 years (Shaquille O'Neal and Tim Duncan).
On February 7, 2023, Trayce Jackson-Davis scored 20 points and posted 18 rebounds in a 66–60 win against Rutgers; he surpassed the 2,000-point mark.
Trayce Jackson-Davis became the first person to win four consecutive Big Ten Player of the Week awards since the award's inception in 1981-82.

In his senior season (2022–23), Trayce Jackson-Davis averaged career bests in points (20.9), rebounds (10.8), assists (4.0), and blocked shots (2.9); he helped lead Indiana to a second-straight NCAA Tournament appearance.
His scoring average marked the highest for a Hoosier since Eric Gordon (in 2007-08).
His rebounding figure was the highest since Steve Downing (in 1972-73).
His block number was the most since Dean Garrett (in 1987-88).

Trayce Jackson-Davis was awarded the Karl Malone Award for the nation's top power forward; he was also named to the Oscar Robertson Trophy Late Season Watch List, the John R. Wooden Men's National Ballot, and the Naismith Trophy Defensive Player of the Year semifinalist list.
TJD was a unanimous choice for the All-Big Ten First Team by the coaches, media, and Associated Press; he collected All-Big Ten Defensive Team honors.

Trayce Jackson-Davis finished his Indiana career as the program's all-time leader in rebounds (1,143) and blocked shots (270); he was third on the all-time scoring list (2,258), and third in double-doubles (50).
Trayce Jackson-Davis played for the United States under-18 basketball team at the 2018 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship; his team won the gold medal.

Trayce Jackson-Davis was drafted 57th overall by the Golden State Warriors in the second round of the 2023 NBA draft. The pick was initially held by the Washington Wizards, who traded the rights to Jackson-Davis for cash considerations on draft night.
Trayce Jackson-Davis made his regular-season debut against the Sacramento Kings on October 27, 2023; he only played 5 minutes and recorded one rebound.
Against the New Orleans Pelicans on October 30, Trayce Jackson-Davis recorded 13 points, 9 rebounds, and 4 blocks in a 130–102 win.
On December 19, Trayce Jackson-Davis achieved his first double-double, recording 10 points, 13 rebounds, and 3 blocks in a 132–126 overtime win against the Boston Celtics.
Trayce Jackson-Davis recorded a second straight double-double against the Washington Wizards on December 22; he had 10 points and 15 rebounds in a 129–118 victory.
Trayce Jackson-Davis recorded 15 points, 6 rebounds, and 4 blocks in a blowout 125-90 win against the Milwaukee Bucks on March 6, with three of those blocks being against Giannis Antetokounmpo.
On April 4, Trayce Jackson-Davis recorded a career-high 20 points combined with 5 rebounds and 4 assists in a 133-110 blowout win against the Houston Rockets.
During the 2023-2024 season, Trayce Jackson-Davis averaged 1.1 blocks per game; this was 4th among rookies.
Trayce Jackson-Davis is the biological son of Dale Davis (former Indiana Pacers power forward/center).
However, he was raised by his mother and stepfather, former NFL running back Raymond Jackson.
Originally, Trayce Jackson-Davis just went by the last name of Davis; however, entering his freshman year of high school, he decided to hyphenate his last name and add "Jackson".
He stated that when he got to high school, he didn't think it was fair. Ray raised him his whole life, so he did Jackson-Davis.
Both Dale Davis and Raymond Jackson want the best out of Trayce; they do this at different angles.
Trayce Jackson-Davis has a sister named Arielle Bellian (née Jackson) and two brothers.

His brother Shaun played basketball in Europe and for the Harlem Globetrotters; his younger brother Tayven Jackson was a high school teammate at Center Grove, and went on to play quarterback in college for the University of Tennessee for one year before transferring to Indiana University.

On March 15, 2019, Trayce Jackson-Davis was honored as the Indiana Gatorade Player of the Year; he received this award not only for his athletic abilities but also for his academic discipline and exemplary character in volunteering locally as a youth basketball coach and at the Wheeler Mission Center in Indianapolis.
